info.title: Sift Sync API
info.description:
Sift is a browser-first RSS reader. This API exposes your subscription state (feeds, read/starred flags), aggregate feed-reading statistics and server-polled items to AI agents and other tools. Agents are first-class sync devices that act with a scoped, revocable credential.

Getting a credential:
- MCP and OAuth clients: use the MCP endpoint at /mcp. Authorisation server metadata is published at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414) and protected resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. The OAuth endpoints are discovered from that metadata and are not described here. The access token is sent as Authorization: Bearer.
- Scripts and the siftctl CLI: open Sift Settings → Agents, create a siftctl pairing code, then redeem the 8-character code with POST /sync/tokens/redeem to obtain a token (23 characters, starts with 't'). Send it in the Authorization: Bearer header.
- Devices: Sift browsers authenticate with the master sync key in the X-Sync-Key header. Agents should not use it.

Security notes:
- Agent credentials carry scopes. `read` allows GET /sync/pull, GET /sync/stats/pull, GET /sync/items and GET /sync/status. `write` additionally allows POST /sync/push. A credential without the required scope receives 403. Each operation below states its scope in `x-required-scope`.
- OAuth access tokens expire after one hour and are renewed by the client with its refresh token. Siftctl tokens do not expire.
- Statistics writes, token management, connection URLs, device codes and account deletion are master-key-only.
- Aggregate statistics contain feed identities, counters, and lifetime-read marker identities only; they do not contain article content or reading-event history.
- A credential grants read or write access to the subscriptions it is bound to. Revoke it anytime from Settings → Agents; revocation takes effect immediately. Rotating the sync key orphans all tokens.
- Writes carry NO timestamps: the server stamps every write with its own monotonic time. Send bare field values.

bearerAuth.description: For agents. An OAuth access token (obtain one through the endpoints advertised at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) or a siftctl token from POST /sync/tokens/redeem, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tokens carry the scopes `read` and `write`, stated per operation in `x-required-scope`. The master sync key is not accepted here.

X-Sync-Key.name: X-Sync-Key
X-Sync-Key.description: For devices. The 22-character master sync key, which grants every scope and is the only credential accepted by the master-key-only operations. Siftctl tokens are also accepted in this header. OAuth access tokens should use the bearer scheme.

FeedPatch.description: A subscription change. All fields are bare values — the server stamps every write, so never send timestamps.

feedId.description: The feed row id. Reuse the feed_id from a pull when the URL is already subscribed; otherwise use the feed URL.

deleted.description: 0 = subscribe/re-subscribe, 1 = unsubscribe (tombstone). Metadata-only pushes omit this field.

FlagPatch.description: A read/starred change for one item. Bare values only.

itemId.description: encodeURIComponent(feedId) + '::' + guid, where guid follows the browser's identity rules (guid ?? id, else link|published, else link).

StatsPatch.description: An approximate observed-volume snapshot. The server derives readOnce from lifetime-read markers; clients must not send a readOnce value.

ReadMarkerPatch.description: A compact lifetime-read marker for one canonical item identity.

itemId.description: Encoded item identity, using the same format as FlagPatch.itemId.

serverTime.description: Monotonic statistics cursor for the next statistics pull.
Monotonic server time. Use as the `since` cursor of your next pull.

feeds.description: Rows with row_at >= since. Tombstoned rows carry deleted=1; filter them out for the live list.

fingerprint.description: 4-char display fingerprint (SHA-256, first 20 bits, Crockford base32).

client_name.description: OAuth client name; null for paired tokens.

items.description: True when server-side polling is enabled and GET /sync/items is available.

post.summary: Exchange an agent pairing code for a token
post.description: Public. For siftctl and HTTP scripts; MCP clients use OAuth instead. The code comes from Sift Settings → Agents and is minted by POST /sync/tokens. One-time use, 5-minute expiry. The returned token is 23 characters, starts with 't', never expires, and holds both `read` and `write`.

get.description: Returns feeds and flags with row_at >= since, plus the new serverTime to use as the next cursor. since=0 returns everything. Agent credentials need the `read` scope (403 without it). Responses are Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous pull's serverTime; 0 for the full dump.

429.description: Rate limited (per sync key, or per token for OAuth tokens)

post.description: PATCH semantics with bare values — the server stamps every write with its own monotonic time. Sending a legacy {value, at} shape is rejected with 400. Agent credentials need the `write` scope (403 without it). Rows are delivered to devices in arrival order via pull.

429.description: Rate limited (per sync key, or per token for OAuth tokens)

post.summary: Push aggregate feed-reading statistics (master key only)
post.description: Pushes approximate observed-volume snapshots and compact once-read marker identities. The server derives readOnce atomically from ever-read state and returns marker acknowledgements plus authoritative affected aggregates. Agent credentials are rejected.

401.description: Missing, revoked, invalid, or agent-token credential

get.description: Returns aggregate rows and lifetime-read marker identities with row_at >= since. Uses an independent statistics cursor and contains no article content or event history. Agent credentials need the `read` scope.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Statistics cursor from the previous response; 0 for the full baseline.

post.description: Idempotent user creation. Agent credentials are rejected with 401.

delete.summary: Delete the account and all its server-side data (master-key only)
delete.description: Deletes the user row and every row keyed by the sync key in one transaction: feeds (including tombstones), flags, feed statistics, agent tokens, pairing codes and the per-key rate-limit counters. Agent tokens and pairing codes stop working immediately, and when server polling is enabled, polled feed URLs and items that no other account subscribes to are removed. A repeat request returns 401 because the key no longer exists. Agent tokens are rejected with 401.

401.description: Invalid, unknown (including already deleted) or token credential

429.description: Rate limited (10 per hour per sync key)

post.summary: Mint a device pairing code (master-key only)
post.description: Issues an 8-character code another Sift browser redeems to join the sync group. Agent tokens are rejected with 401 — a device code redeems to the master key.

post.summary: Exchange a device pairing code for the sync key (for Sift browsers)
post.description: Public, for the Sift device-pairing flow only. Agent pairing codes are NOT accepted here — use POST /sync/tokens/redeem.

200.description: Sync key (master credential — treat as secret)

get.description: Returns the short fingerprint Settings shows for the sync group, so an agent can confirm which account it is bound to. Any valid agent credential works; no particular scope is required.

Returns items retained by server-side polling for the caller's live subscriptions, up to the per-account polling cap, paginated by insertion sequence. Items are kept for seven days. Available only when polling is enabled (see GET /sync/capabilities); otherwise 404. Agent credentials need the `read` scope. Responses are Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from the previous response; 0 starts from the beginning.

cursor.description: Pass as `after` on the next request.

more.description: True when another page is available.

429.description: Rate limited (per sync key, or per token for OAuth tokens)

post.summary: Mint a single-use connection URL (master-key only)
post.description: Creates a connection ID, valid for ten minutes, bound to this sync group. The returned URL (<origin>/mcp/c/<connectionId>) is pasted into an MCP client as a custom connector. The client then discovers OAuth through /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and the user approves with one Allow on the consent page, which consumes the ID. The URL is a bearer secret until it is used or expires. Agent credentials are rejected with 401.

url.description: The MCP URL to give the client.

429.description: Rate limited (20 per hour per sync key)

post.summary: Mint an agent pairing code (master-key only)
post.description: Issues an 8-character code, valid for five minutes, that POST /sync/tokens/redeem exchanges for a revocable siftctl token. MCP and OAuth clients do not use this route; they connect through POST /sync/connections or OAuth discovery. Agent credentials are rejected with 401.

get.description: Metadata only — raw tokens are never returned. Lists siftctl tokens (origin `paired`) and OAuth grants (origin `oauth`), one row per grant. OAuth grants show the client name and granted scopes; use `label` for a user-chosen name and the fingerprint to match a token shown by your tool.

patch.summary: Rename an agent token or OAuth grant (master-key only)
patch.description: Sets the display label. An empty string clears it. Labels are trimmed and at most 64 characters.

delete.summary: Revoke an agent token or OAuth grant (master-key only)
delete.description: Revocation is immediate. For an OAuth grant, the access and refresh tokens are deleted together and the agent must be connected again.
